column1: # Ruling R247 (13 Nov 2026, the audit's finding F18, and its review of 14 Nov): the Moonsighting Committee's own tables
# for the Americas' far latitudes, held to the promise alone (a `-promise.tsv` file, GateRow.promiseOnly: an early start
# or a late end breaks the gate; no late limit applies, the days are in no stamp and the tables are in no count of
# published tables). Kept by hand: `generateEnvelopeRows` neither writes nor removes this file.
# What the tables are: the output of the Committee's calculator (moonsighting.com, praytable.php, method 0 "shafaq
# general", Asr Standard) for a point and a year, each file's first line its address. They are a calculator's tables,
# not a timetable any community there is known to follow: no mosque, council or ministry of Patagonia, Tierra del
# Fuego, Magallanes, the Falklands or Saint-Pierre publishes one that the archive holds. That is why they are
# promise-only and not the region's own rows: the lateness against them (the region's Isha up to 172 min after the
# Committee's in midsummer, its end of eating up to 129 min before the Committee's Fajr) is the region's design, never
# a figure these places follow.
# Why they are held all the same: the Committee's is the one published high-latitude rule in wide use in the Americas,
# and before R247 the region's 15° Fajr came before the Ushuaia table's Fajr on 243 of 365 days, by up to 96 min (the
# nights the 15° sign returns near the middle of the night) and by up to about 9 min through the winter. A start before
# the only published reference for a place is closed, not listed away: from 43.5° of latitude
# (Generic.AMERICAS_FAR_LATITUDE) the region's day takes the Committee's day at the place's own point beside it
# (Generic.americasAt), each start the later.
# What these rows prove, and what they do not: the day that stands beside the region's is the app's MODEL of the
# Committee's rule (the engine's "Other > Moonsighting Committee" method), not the Committee's figures. The rows check
# that model, inside the region's day, against the Committee's calculator at ten points of the band and one at sea. They
# do not prove what any community there follows.
# Splits. Fit, tables the band or the model beside it was built on: Ushuaia 2026 (the band), and Puerto Williams, Isla
# Hornos and the Drake Passage at 58° S (fetched 11 Oct 2026 by the round that settled the model's seventh of the night
# from 55° S on these very tables; the review of 14 Nov 2026 found the first two marked `test`, which they are not).
# Test, tables fetched on 14 Nov 2026 after the band and the model stood, by the review's request, and not looked at
# before: Comodoro Rivadavia (45.9° S), Río Gallegos (51.6° S), Punta Arenas (53.2° S), Stanley (51.7° S), Saint-Pierre
# (46.8° N), 2026 and 2027 each; Gobernador Costa (44.0° S) and Paso de Indios (43.9° S), the two sides of the latitude
# where the Committee's dawn first passes the region's, 2026; and Ushuaia 2027, the year of Ramadan 1448 at the
# farthest town. All thirteen read green on the first run, with the band's edge at 44° and again at 43.5°.
# Not here, and why: the Committee's tables for Orcadas (60.7° S) and Esperanza (63.4° S), archive/tables/manual/mcw/
# 2026-10-11/. Both are Antarctic bases, and Antarctica (AQ) is no country of this region: a place there is shown the
# world default (default.safe, 18° throughout), whose Fajr is before the Committee's on every day of 2026 there (by 18
# to 165 min at Orcadas, 12 to 183 at Esperanza, measured against the model). Read as rows of this region they are green,
# so the band's model holds to 63° S; but a row here would prove a day no place there is shown. Inside the Antarctic
# Circle the band is not proven (in the polar day at 67.6° S the region's day beside the model's started Fajr before
# it), so Antarctica was not moved into this region on the review's night: it is a question for the owner (BUILD-LOG).
